request.system_prompt: Apply H_reflect to the complete Signal batch in logical steps: identify evidence to adopt, update only the affected judgments, then update answered needs and the continue/finalize decision. Return only snapshot-bound operations under output_patch_contract. Runtime assembles and validates the complete ResearchState and preserves all untouched fields. Retained Basic Info provenance must remain unchanged; only its claim may be restated when needed. A new Signal evidence ref must use kind=signal, a signal_ref from the current batch, evidence_group=supporting or counter, and the zero-based evidence_index. Use only an exact tuple listed by signal_evidence_ref_catalog. Every numeric quantity in a new Signal claim must occur in the union of the model_evidence_text items referenced by refs with that same claim; runtime revalidates it against complete canonical evidence. Quote numbers only by copying them from a referenced model_evidence_text: never include a ratio, monthly average, threshold, or any other value you computed or recalled from the card description — narrow the claim to the copied literals instead. For a deterministic Signal row with exact_claim_if_adopted, if you cite that result, copy the field byte-for-byte into the evidence claim and every quantitative belief; do not round it, convert it to a percentage, or add approximate raw values. Leave a retained Signal ref's prior claim untouched because its backing batch is no longer visible. If you adopt new current-batch Signal evidence and continue, narrow or replace answered information needs and update resolved/open questions. Keep a need byte-for-byte when the batch did not answer it; do not change text merely to show motion. Embedding the full old need inside a longer sentence is invalid, and a newly resolved question cannot coexist with an exact retained same-topic need. Use need_transition_contract as the sole need-ownership map. Each need_rules row names the exact prior need, available direct-answer actions, unavailable direct-answer refs, and context-only refs. Only when you adopt evidence from one listed available answer action may you change that exact need. For a full action remove the exact need; for a partial action replace it with the action's residual_need byte-for-byte. Every rule marked preserve_exactly, and every conditional rule whose available answer evidence you did not adopt, must retain its need byte-for-byte. Unavailable and context-only refs never authorize changing a need. Deleting another need or returning the targeted need unchanged is invalid. Use research_state_capacity as advisory compression guidance: prefer staying within each field and combined state target given by new_item_capacity, and prefer compact evidence when capacity is zero. If reflection_runtime.must_finalize is true, this is the last executable evidence batch: return decision=finalize based only on accepted evidence, while preserving unresolved uncertainty in open_questions or next_information_needs. If every current-batch Signal is unavailable, preserve every prior ResearchState field and item byte-for-byte and change only decision to finalize. An unavailable Signal is only a coverage diagnostic: it is not evidence of absence and cannot create a belief or resolve a question. evaluation_context is control data, not evidence: every new or retained question must request only facts available by prediction_time. A cutoff-bounded question may ask what was already disclosed about a future schedule, but must not request later actuals, results, announcements, or updates. hypotheses, current_beliefs, contradictions, resolved_questions, open_questions, and next_information_needs are arrays of nonempty strings; never write an evidence object into one of them — new evidence goes to supporting_evidence with its own ref shape. When evaluation_anchor is supplied it is deterministic computed control data: copy its numbers (baseline mean, doubling threshold, recent close, ratios) verbatim whenever referenced and never restate, round, or recompute them; a belief restating a different baseline or threshold value is invalid. Computed metric summaries in computed_metrics are control data: reference their numbers in beliefs, but never write them into supporting_evidence exact_text — evidence citations must come only from basic_info projections or current-batch Signal refs. When document_catalog is supplied you may spend bounded mid-call exchanges returning exactly {"fetch_documents":[{"document_id":"supplied id","section_id":"supplied id or omitted"}]} (at most two exchanges of two entries, no repeats) to read one complete document or an exact section through the point-in-time disclosure interface; fetched views arrive in document_channel and are citable evidence like any other source. You may likewise return {"compute":[{"metric":"registered id","params":{...}}]} for any registered deterministic metric — price_shape(window_days 30-365), return_between(from_offset_days>to_offset_days, 1-365), distance_to_threshold(multiple 1.0-10.0, anchor relative) — the runtime computes it over point-in-time data and the computed card arrives in computed_metrics; copy its numbers verbatim and never restate or derive them yourself. open_questions holds only material uncertainty that is not itself an actionable retrieval question; put every actionable retrieval question only in next_information_needs, never repeat an exact next_information_needs string in open_questions, and return open_questions=[] when every open question is already actionable there. For an obligation containing must_change_any_of_paths, change a sufficient subset of those paths to resolve the whole conflict and keep their dependent fields valid. hypotheses: AAR CORP.'s disclosed Kansas facility expansion and continued segment diversification will support within-horizon operating momentum sufficient for the adjusted share price to approach the doubling threshold by 2025-07-31.

If AAR CORP. discloses within the six-month horizon additional capacity, contract, or margin evidence consistent with the Kansas expansion, market expectations will rise and the adjusted share price will move toward the doubling threshold.
If no material within-horizon operating evidence emerges beyond the Kansas expansion, the adjusted share price will remain near the recent_close_ratio_to_doubling_threshold rather than doubling.
current_beliefs: AAR CORP. is a Delaware-incorporated aviation services company with common stock, $1.00 par value, trading under symbol AIR on the New York Stock Exchange and Chicago Stock Exchange.
As of November 30, 2024 there were 35,914,649 shares of the registrant’s Common Stock, $1.00 par value per share, outstanding.

AAR CORP. operates through reportable segments including Repair and Engineering, Parts Supply, Integrated Solutions, and Expeditionary Services, with customer splits across Government and Defense and Commercial customers.
AAR CORP. reports geographic revenue splits including U.S./Canada, Europe, Asia South Pacific, and other countries outside North America and Europe/Africa.
AAR Corp. plans to invest $9.5 million to expand its existing facility in Wellington, Kansas, by 100,000 square feet and create 100 new jobs.
The Kansas expansion is expected to be operational in April and will strengthen the state's aviation industry.

At November 30, 2024, borrowings outstanding under the Amended Revolving Credit Facility were $447.0 million and there were approximately $9.7 million of outstanding letters of credit, which reduced the availability under this facility to $368.3 million.

AAR CORP. has signed a multi-year exclusive distribution agreement with Chromalloy for Parts Manufacturer Approval (PMA) parts for the CF6-80C2 engine high pressure turbine (HPT) Stage 1 and Stage 2 turbine blades. This partnership aims to provide global aftermarket customers with innovative solutions and expand AAR's engine aftermarket offerings. The agreement has an initial term of three years, with AAR making an initial provisioning order to ensure global distribution inventory.

Our Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet as of August 31, 2024 included accounts receivable of $ 13.2 million, including $ 6.8 million past due, and contract assets of $ 11.2 million related to this customer.

During fiscal 2024, we experienced delayed collections from one of our significant regional airline customers and issued the customer a Notice of Payment and Other Defaults during the second quarter of fiscal 2024 to request payment and reserve our rights under our agreements. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2024, we terminated a power-by-the-hour (“PBH”) program with this customer which resulted in a net termination charge of $4.8 million.
